crime_highlights: Tyere shared a handgun with Malik
went back into Vincent’s home, created a confrontation with Vincent who was passed out on a couch, and, when Vincent got up to engage with Tyere, Tyere shot him in the head
Tyere left Vincent’s house without offering any medical assistance
found Vincent Beals sleeping peacefully on his own couch, provoked him, and shot him in the head
rationale_highlights: The IRCA reveals numerous challenges in Mr. Brushett’s background
considering the mitigating factor of his very challenging background as described in the IRCA
I agree with the Crown that the appropriate period for parole ineligibility is 13 years

crime_highlights: Mr. Whynder-Ewing arrived at approximately 1:00 a.m. He was, at that time, in possession of a loaded handgun on his person.
responded by taking his own loaded gun and shooting Mr. Thomas five times. All five shots perforated Mr. Thomas’ body, causing his death.
rationale_highlights: Mr. Whynder-Ewing is an African Nova Scotian

The moral culpability of an African Nova Scotian offender has to be assessed in the context of historic factors and systemic racism, as was done in this case. The African Nova Scotian offender's background and social context may have a mitigating effect on moral blameworthiness.
I took these limitations into account.
note: Para 13 is long; para 15 states the sentence reduction for race and culture.

crime_highlights: Mr. Willis broke into her home through a basement window in the middle of the night and proceeded to choke Ms. Harding to death with a pair of her jeans
She was completely defenceless in her own home against the onslaught of violence she encountered in the early morning hours of July 10, 2020
Ms. Harding’s dead body was left on the hallway floor, only to be discovered by her son, Mark Harding, more than a day later
After killing Ms. Harding, Mr. Willis ransacked her bedroom, stole her personal belongings
rationale_highlights: The Court is mindful of our Court of Appeal’s words
background and social context may have a mitigating effect on moral blameworthiness
Mr. Willis has endured racial discrimination as a black man living in Nova Scotia as well as other parts of the country
I am mindful of the points raised in the IRCA
note: Court never clearly states IRCA reduced culpability or sentence.
